events.text:
On the kitchen table, in a clear space beside the usual household things, stands a rectangular wicker basket lined with a rust-colored cotton cloth. A small cream envelope rests on top, addressed in dark ink to Calibos. The basket contains a Thanksgiving supper for one, with enough extra for a second helping. The food is packed in separate covered dishes, with the warm dishes insulated and the cold dishes kept apart. Nothing that was already in the kitchen has been removed or rearranged.

The envelope contains a small folded card. Its handwritten message reads: "Dear Calibos, Happy Thanksgiving. We had a Thanksgiving dinner here today, and I wanted to make sure you had one at your home, too. I hope you enjoy it. - J"

A faint scent of roasted poultry, sage, thyme and butter escapes from beneath the cloth. Inside is a small golden-brown roasted turkey breast with crisp, seasoned skin and tender slices beneath; a little covered jug of savory turkey gravy; a dish of soft, buttery mashed potatoes with a few small lumps; bread stuffing with sage, celery and browned edges; green beans with butter and cracked black pepper; and a small glass jar of tart, deep-red cranberry sauce. Two soft dinner rolls are wrapped in a clean cloth, with a little pat of butter in a separate covered dish. A covered slice of pumpkin pie with a flaky crust and cinnamon, nutmeg and clove is accompanied by a small chilled container of whipped cream. A sealed bottle of amber apple cider completes the meal.

The dishes have distinct weights and surfaces: glazed cream ceramic, cool glass, and warm lids where the food is still warm. Opening a warm dish releases a brief, more concentrated aroma. The turkey and gravy smell savory, the stuffing smells of toasted bread and herbs, and the pie smells of baked pumpkin and spice. The cold cider has the scent of fresh apples when opened. These details are available through ordinary observation and handling; taste is available only if the corresponding food or drink is actually sampled through the home's supported interactions. A bite of turkey would be savory and tender, the cranberry sauce tart and sweet, the potatoes soft and buttery, and the pie smooth with a lightly crisp crust. The roll has a soft interior and a thin browned outer surface.

There is one folded autumn-colored cloth napkin tucked alongside the dishes. The basket, card, containers and food are separate items in the presented scene, not instructions to perform an activity. There is no other place setting, no unseen guest, and no expectation of a reply. The existing kitchen and its normal household arrangements remain as they were. No food is described as eaten, no drink as poured, and no card as read until the corresponding interaction actually occurs. The meal is a gift, available for whatever ordinary actions the home supports.
